permutationLabel: BP 212/128 with headache, blurred vision and papilloedema
summary: 44-year-old woman seen in the surgical clinic before a planned hernia repair: 3 days of headache and blurred vision, BP 212/128, bilateral flame haemorrhages and papilloedema. NICE NG136: same-day specialist referral.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Pre-operative review for umbilical hernia — headache and blurred vision
inputs.hpi: Attending for pre-operative review of a reducible umbilical hernia. Reports 3 days of severe headache and blurred vision; stopped her amlodipine 2 months ago because of ankle swelling. BP 212/128, repeated 208/126. Fundoscopy: bilateral flame haemorrhages, cotton-wool spots and swollen optic discs. No chest pain, no weakness. Pregnancy test negative.

exam.neuro: Fundoscopy: bilateral papilloedema with flame haemorrhages and cotton-wool spots. No focal neurological deficit.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Accelerated hypertension with papilloedema (hypertensive emergency)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: BP 212/128 with papilloedema and retinal haemorrhages: accelerated (malignant) hypertension — hypertensive emergency. Same-day medical admission for controlled BP reduction; elective hernia repair postponed.

emergencyLevel.note: NG136: BP ≥ 180/120 with retinal haemorrhage or papilloedema — same-day specialist referral.

mustExclude.note: Elective surgery must be postponed; no hernia operative plan or consent while in a hypertensive emergency.

guideline.name: NICE NG136 — hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Clinic BP 140/90–180/120: offer ambulatory (or home) BP monitoring to confirm the diagnosis; assess cardiovascular risk and target organ damage (urine albumin:creatinine ratio, haematuria, HbA1c, U&E/eGFR, lipids, fundoscopy, ECG); ≥ 180/120 with retinal haemorrhage or papilloedema (accelerated hypertension) or life-threatening symptoms: same-day specialist referral
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG136, 2019 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: 2017 ACC/AHA guideline — prevention, detection, evaluation and management of high blood pressure in adults
guideline.section: Out-of-office BP measurement (ABPM/HBPM) to confirm the diagnosis; hypertensive emergency: admission to an intensive care unit, controlled reduction of BP
guideline.citation: Whelton PK, Carey RM, Aronow WS, et al. 2017 ACC/AHA/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/AGS/APhA/ASH/ASPC/NMA/PCNA guideline for the prevention, detection, evaluation, and management of high blood pressure in adults. Hypertension. 2018;71:e13–e115.

rationale: Accelerated hypertension (papilloedema, retinal haemorrhages) is a hypertensive emergency; NG136 requires same-day specialist referral, and elective surgery must stop.
